clue.text: Song and dance and poor ratings after each class

indicators.note: the reworked letters are placed after the words for each and class

parts.note: per means each, as in so much per head
a form is a school class

indicators.note: poor suggests the ratings are in a bad state, so their letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A show's song-and-dance routine gets bad ratings after every class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' turns RATINGS into INGARTS, which 'after' places behind PER and FORM.
explanation.definitionFit: Song and dance are among the stage disciplines performed live before an audience.

clue.text: Speak fast

explanation.surface: An instruction to talk quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak a view is to voice it outright, and a fast train that skips stops is called by the same word.

clue.text: See 15
Backtrack about the FT being contrary

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to recant is to retract or backtrack on a statement
the paper speaking of itself would say us

explanation.surface: Someone reverses position on the Financial Times out of sheer contrariness.
explanation.walkthrough: In its own crossword the FT is 'us'; 'about' puts RECANT round US.
explanation.definitionFit: A recusant refuses to comply with authority, a stubbornly contrary person.

clue.text: Why Le Monde matters to Macron

definitions.text: Why Le Monde matters to Macron

parts.words: Why Le Monde matters to Macron
parts.note: the French paper's title translates literally as the planet's name, so it would be supremely important to the French president

explanation.surface: A question about why the French president cares about a leading Paris newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for something of supreme personal importance, and Le Monde translates as that global term.

clue.text: Reptiles vacantly gaze and check onlookers

indicators.note: vacantly means emptied of their insides, leaving only each word's first and last letters

explanation.surface: Lizards stare blankly while spectators watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Geckos are small lizards, which are reptiles.

clue.text: See 1
Are they perhaps asleep? Not when a lion's about!

definitions.text: Are they perhaps asleep? Not when a lion's about!

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of the two words are moved around into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Grazing animals may doze, but not with a predator prowling nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' shuffles ASLEEP and NOT together; the whole clue also describes the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Antelopes are grazing animals that a lion hunts, so they stay alert when one is near.

clue.text: Idiot the electorate really starts to follow on this?

definitions.text: Idiot the electorate really starts to follow on this?

parts.note: a twit is a foolish person

indicators.note: starts means taking the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A wry dig that a fool posts and the voters actually follow along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' places the initials of 'the electorate really' after TWIT, and the whole clue hints at a social platform.
explanation.definitionFit: Users follow other accounts on this social media platform, now called X.

clue.text: Some jewellery for lovemate

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
pal is a friend or mate

explanation.surface: A gift of jewellery for a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is a gemstone set in rings and brooches.

clue.text: Cartoons showed space voyage before squadron leader got demoted

indicators.note: demoted means moved lower down, so that letter shifts later in the word

parts.note: cosmic means of outer space

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the leading letter of the word squadron
a trip is a journey or voyage

explanation.surface: A cartoon depicted a space journey before an RAF officer lost rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got demoted' moves the S of COSMIC further down to give COMICS.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic strip is a sequence of cartoon drawings telling a story.

clue.text: See 22
Very dull in hospital department recently

indicators.note: in signals that these words are placed inside the department's letters

parts.note: A&E is the accident and emergency department of a British hospital
so means very, as in so tired
flat means dull or lifeless

explanation.surface: Things have been very dull in the hospital department lately.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British name for a hospital's emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means lately, over the period just past.

clue.text: Without me, don't assume nasty surprises

indicators.note: nasty suggests the letters are messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice not to take things for granted, or you will get unpleasant shocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without me' says ME is taken from the letters of DON'T ASSUME, which 'nasty' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To astound is to amaze or shock, so astounds means surprises.

clue.text: Reportedly banned from major chest radiotherapy

indicators.note: from signals the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone is barred from a major course of chest radiation treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a band, and 'band' sounds like 'banned'; 'Reportedly' signals that sound pun in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large musical band, and band sounds like banned.

clue.text: Artistic collection showing stricken fort in the midst of viral illness

indicators.note: in the midst of means placed in the middle of the other word

parts.note: polio is a disease caused by a virus

indicators.note: stricken means struck down or damaged, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An art collection depicts a fort ravaged during an epidemic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stricken' turns FORT into RTFO, which goes into POLIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is a case or set of an artist's works.

clue.text: Calf eating pig's head gets this disease

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a calf is a young bovine, a little ox

indicators.note: head means the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A calf that eats pork catches an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Smallpox is a contagious viral disease, now eradicated.

clue.text: Selection of recipes turned into a poem

indicators.note: turned means the picked letters are read backwards
a selection is a part of the word, picked out of its letters

explanation.surface: A bunch of recipes rewritten in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Selection of' takes CIPE from inside 'recipes', and 'turned' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long narrative poem about heroic deeds.

clue.text: Outline for moving back into big house

indicators.note: into signals one piece placed inside another

parts.note: a pile is a large stately house

indicators.note: moving back means the word for is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A summary of reasons for returning to a mansion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving back' turns FOR into ROF, which 'into' places inside PILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A profile is a side outline of a face or a brief sketch.

clue.text: Some strange country bumpkin outside missing his family

indicators.note: outside means this word goes round the other

parts.note: a hick is an unsophisticated rural person

indicators.note: strange signals the letters are put in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A weird rustic left out in the cold pines for his relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' turns SOME into OMES, which goes inside HICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Being homesick is longing for one's own household and kin while away.

clue.text: A little heat round oven by the seaside

indicators.note: round means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: cal, the calorie, is a small unit of heat
an oast is a kiln or oven for drying hops

explanation.surface: Gentle warmth around a stove at a beach house.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast is a hop-drying kiln found in Kent, south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Coastal means by the shore, near the sea.

clue.text: Well or hard, but not good

definitions.text: Well or hard, but not good

parts.words: Well or hard, but not good
parts.note: the words well and hard can modify verbs, whereas good is only an adjective in standard usage

explanation.surface: A verdict that something is fine or tough but not quite good.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb is the part of speech modifying a verb, as well and hard do.

clue.text: Darling, bananas seldom new fruit

parts.note: honey is an affectionate term like darling

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A loved one, gone mad, rarely gets new fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' rearranges SELDOM NEW into DEWMELONS; the fruit theme makes 'bananas' look like part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Honeydew melons are sweet green-fleshed fruits.

clue.text: All the nuts? Deadly

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Is everyone mad? Deadly so.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethal means fatal, capable of causing death.

clue.text: See 5
Tear possibly caused by doctor engaged in minor procedure

indicators.note: engaged in means this piece is placed inside the others

parts.note: little means small or minor
op is short for operation, a surgical procedure

explanation.surface: A rip produced by a doctor during a small operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' looks like a rip, but it is a drop from the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A tear, as wept, is a small bead of liquid.

clue.text: This could be the top twenty

definitions.text: This could be the top twenty

parts.words: This could be the top twenty
parts.note: a chart of the twenty best-selling records is made up of popular successes

explanation.surface: A remark about the music chart.
explanation.definitionFit: The top twenty consists of the best-selling chart songs, each a popular success.

clue.text: A role model doesn't put down a poor past lover more than necessary

parts.note: to set something is to put it down
bad means poor in quality
an ex is a former partner
ample means plentiful, more than enough

explanation.surface: An exemplary person refuses to belittle an old flame beyond reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't' belongs to the definition: what a role model avoids.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving so others copy one's misconduct is the opposite of being a role model.
